precepts.text: Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments. Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers. Why? Because we would forget who we are; we would lose our way; and he is going to turn us back to our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
precepts.point: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in. Now, you may think initially it is talking about John the Baptist; that is a good thought, but it is actually talking about the John the Baptist work in the last days.
precepts.why:
“Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me”. You may think at first that is only John the Baptist. That is a good thought, but it is the John the Baptist work in the last days, and the end of Malachi shows it.

“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” Then here it comes: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”. That is still the John the Baptist work, but in the last days it is Elijah, sent before that great and dreadful day.

What would he do? “And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children”. Why? Because we would forget who we are. We would lose our way. “And the heart of the children to their fathers”: he is going to show us our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and turn us back to them, “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

So the messenger of Malachi 3 is the messenger sent before the Lord comes to his temple in the last days, to bring a people who forgot themselves back to their fathers and their law before the day of his coming.

precepts.text: This is what the refiner's fire and the soap mean. And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die: two out of every three of our people shall be cut off. But the third shall be left therein; and I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, The Lord is my God. That is the wilderness right there.
precepts.point: But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' soap. That is how you know it is the last days.
precepts.why:
“For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ soap”. Christ is like a refiner's fire. Zechariah shows what that fire and that soap mean.

“And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”. Two out of every three of our people shall be cut off and die. Why? Because we know damn good and well.

“But the third shall be left therein.” There is going to be a third: one third will be saved out of this land, America. “And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. That is the refiner sitting over the silver in Malachi 3, purging the sons of Levi “as gold and silver”.

“They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.” That is the wilderness right there. That is how you know Malachi 3 is the last days: “who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?” Only the third part that comes through the fire refined.

precepts.text: For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the Lord of hosts. That is the offering of Judah and Jerusalem.
precepts.point: And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness. Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in former years.
precepts.why:
Malachi 3 ends with the refined people offering again: “Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in former years.” What is the offering of Judah and Jerusalem? Malachi already said it in the first chapter.

“For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the Lord of hosts.”

Incense offered unto his name, and a pure offering. That is the offering in righteousness that the purified sons of Levi will offer after the Lord sits as a refiner and purifier of silver: a pure offering, with his name great from the rising of the sun to the going down of it.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
precepts.point: And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers.
precepts.why:
“And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers”. That is what we wanted to get to. The law already said what God thinks of sorcery: “Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.”

Look at what our people are doing. Growing numbers of black women in Maryland and across the nation are leaving church worship for what they call ancient forms of spiritual contact. Some call it witchcraft, a term they accept and embrace, offering prayers to spirits and deities like Oshun. More than two hundred witches gathered at a convention in Baltimore. They grew up Christian, Baptist, Episcopal, a grandfather a preacher, a father a deacon, and now they call themselves witches. God said he is going to be a swift witness against the sorcerers.

A sister who used crystals testified that instead of healing you, it entices you and traps you into depending on it for every little thing; it is like a placebo effect. So brothers, be careful. Sisters come in with these crystals and say, oh no, it’s just spirituality. It is witchcraft. Don’t fall for it, or you are going to have demons all up in your house.

precepts.text: If a man be found lying with a woman married to an husband, then they shall both of them die: so shalt thou put away evil from Israel. At the sit down, the Christian pastors could not explain adultery.
precepts.why:
“and against the adulterers”. What is adultery? When the brothers had the sit down, the Christian pastors could not explain adultery. The law explains it: “If a man be found lying with a woman married to an husband, then they shall both of them die, both the man that lay with the woman, and the woman: so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.”

A site advertises connecting with swingers of color, black swingers in the lifestyle. This is adultery.

And it happened among us. In San Antonio a sister bought another sister lingerie to spice up her marriage, and invited her and her husband over. They switched partners, and it went on for months without anyone knowing. It only came out when one wife decided she wanted the other husband. The husband left without a wife got mad, and then he revealed it, as if the Holy Spirit came on him. You didn’t reveal it because a spirit told you to; you revealed it because you were mad.

We had to put him out; everybody had to go. Now that brother is on YouTube and TikTok like an all knowing teacher, teaching everything we teach, but he is not going to reveal that he was that swinger brother. God said he will be a swift witness against the adulterers, and so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.

precepts.text: And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord. That goes into perjury and false statements.
precepts.why:
“and against false swearers”. What is a false swearer? “And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.”

That goes into perjury and false statements. To swear by his name falsely is to profane the name of our God.

So when God comes near to judgment, he will be a swift witness against the ones who lie under oath and make false statements, the same as against the sorcerers and the adulterers. He is the Lord; he signs the command with his own name, and he will not let his name be profaned.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning.
precepts.point: And against those that oppress the hireling in his wages. You might say to yourself, this does not apply to us, nobody among us oppresses the hireling in his wages. Oh, you would be shocked; it took place right here. Brothers with their own trucking authority hired the brothers, then gave the good, high paying jobs to the ones they liked, gave the others little work, and paid brothers late and unequal. Everything was unjust.
precepts.why:
“and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages”. You might say to yourself, this does not apply to us; nobody among us oppresses the hireling in his wages. Oh, you would be shocked. It took place right here.

The brothers said, let’s all be truckers. Some got their own authority: I control all this, I’ll hire you, and you, and you. But I like these brothers better, so I’m giving you the good, high paying jobs, and the rest of you I’m not giving too much work.

“Thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning.”

Some brothers were being paid late, and were not getting paid the same amount. Everything was unjust. That is defrauding your neighbour and robbing him, and it is exactly what Malachi says God will be a swift witness against. Don’t get mad; get glad, and get it right.

precepts.text: Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child. If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry; and my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
precepts.why:
“and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless”. The law on the widow and the fatherless is heavy: “Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child. If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry”.

“And my wrath shall wax hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.” Damn. Whoever afflicts the widow and the fatherless, God makes his own wife a widow and his own children fatherless.

Then Malachi finishes: “For I am the Lord, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.” The same God who wrote these laws has not changed, and he still judges the sorcerers, the adulterers, the false swearers and the oppressors. And because he changes not, the sons of Jacob are not consumed. That is why we are still in existence today, the twelve tribes.

precepts.text: They that feared the Most High spake often one to another, a safety net of communication so our conversations stay in the law.
precepts.point: Where should we make our refuge? It begins with meditating on the scriptures, which is why the four chapters a day has been set up.
precepts.why:
“Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.” They that feared the Most High spoke often one to another, and he heard it and wrote a book of remembrance for them.

That speaking often one to another is a safety net of communication, so our conversations stay in the law. Meditating on the scriptures day and night and talking them over with the brethren is how we make our refuge in the shadow of his wings until the calamities be overpast.

precepts.text: Tithes are meat for the storehouse, not money; when the nation is righteous He rebukes the devourer so it destroys not the fruit of the ground.
precepts.point: He smote all the firstborn, the chief of all their strength. The firstborn is the chief of one's strength, as Reuben was Jacob's strength before he lost it.

note.label: Psalm 105: Remember His Marvelous Works from Abraham to the Exodus

precepts.why:
“He spake, and the locusts came, and caterpillers, and that without number, And did eat up all the herbs in their land, and devoured the fruit of their ground.” That is the devourer, and in Malachi the Most High promises to rebuke it for the sake of a righteous nation: “I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the field”.

“Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me. But ye say, Wherein have we robbed thee? In tithes and offerings. Ye are cursed with a curse: for ye have robbed me, even this whole nation.” The tithe is “meat in mine house”: “Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house”. Tithes are meat for the storehouse, not money.

What fell on Egypt as a plague is what the Most High holds back from a righteous nation. When the nation is righteous he rebukes the devourer so that it does not destroy the fruit of the ground; he opens the windows of heaven and pours out a blessing “that there shall not be room enough to receive it.”

precepts.text: A book of remembrance was written for those that feared the Most High and thought upon his name, which is the same thing read back in verse one.
precepts.point: Surely he shall not be moved forever; the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.

note.label: Psalm 112: Blessed Is the Man That Feareth the Most High

precepts.why:
“the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.” Malachi shows where that remembrance is kept: “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another: and the Lord hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name.”

A book of remembrance was written for those that feared the Most High and thought upon his name. That is the same thing read back in verse one of this psalm, the man that feareth the Lord; he shall not be moved for ever, and he is in everlasting remembrance before the Lord.

precepts.text: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.
precepts.point: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judea, saying repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. He is the messenger the prophets said would go before the Lord, coming in the spirit of Elijah.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness of Judea, “Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” He is the messenger the prophets said would go before the Lord: “Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me”.

Malachi says that after the messenger prepares the way, “the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in”. John is the messenger sent ahead; the Lord who follows him is Christ, the messenger of the covenant. John's preaching of repentance in the wilderness is the preparing of that way.

precepts.text: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me; and he is like a refiner's fire.
precepts.point: John is the messenger written of, sent before the face of the Lord to prepare the way.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
“What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?” Not a reed shaken with the wind, nor a man in soft clothing, for “they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses”, but a prophet, “and more than a prophet. For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.”

The writing is Malachi: “Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in”. John is that messenger, sent before the face of the Lord to prepare the way, and the Lord who comes suddenly to his temple behind him is Christ.

Malachi goes on: “But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ soap: And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness.” The one the messenger prepares the way for is a refiner's fire; he purifies and purges. That is what came behind John, and it is why John was more than a prophet.

note.label: Know Your Enemy: God's Foes & Ours

points: Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another. When you are getting tried, there is another element the Lord is showing you: a lot of brothers and sisters like to suffer in silence, and the Lord is showing you your communication is weak and you need to grow in that area. He is giving us lifelines; we have to use them.

Spake often one to another is not, I only speak to you on the Sabbath. We ask brothers, how are you doing; I am good, I am enduring. That was an opportunity right there, and you played games with it. And you are really not suffering in silence, because we see the spirit on you. We ask, are you okay, sister? I am okay. You look bugged out completely; are you all right? Because of pride we suffer in silence, then start being offended with everybody around us, and next thing you know you find yourself out the door: they do not really love me, where is the charity? That is how brothers and sisters go down.
According to Christians, God can change; it is a new day now. Let me show you what the Bible says: for I am the Lord, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.

You know what that verse is saying? The reason the Israelites are still alive is because God does not change. If he changed, we would have been consumed. The same God who chose Israel to be his people is the same God today, yesterday, and forever. He does not evolve.
